comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims C1-C10. Both accept these experimental observations from the literature as valid context. OpenEval notes they provide empirical foundation; peer reviewers implicitly accept them by noting the paper explains contradictory experimental results.

Disagreement on theoretical framework claims C11-C13. OpenEval finds them supported with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, specifically questioning whether results depend on gradient descent versus general loss minimization, requesting this as an essential revision.

Strong agreement on selectivity increase claims C14, C18-C21 (with C36 also in peer result). Both treat robustness of selectivity increase as a core, well-supported contribution. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'compelling evidence' and a 'valuable finding.'

Agreement on correlation behavior claims C22-C26. OpenEval finds them supported by simulation data. Peer reviewers accept parameter-dependent correlations as a key finding that reconciles experimental observations. Peer result also includes C15, C27-C30 showing broader grouping of correlation-related claims.

Agreement on geometric interpretation claims C27-C30. OpenEval finds them supported by simulation data and consistent with experiments. Peer reviewers group these with other correlation claims (C15, C22-C26) and accept them as demonstrating parameter-dependent selectivity profiles.

Partial disagreement on mathematical framework claims C31, C34, C36. OpenEval finds them supported by mathematical analysis. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about mechanistic explanations (C31, C34, C62-C63, C67-C71), requesting 'more intuitive explanations' for context selectivity emergence.

Perfect agreement on parameter dependency claims C41-C42, C44-C45. Both accept these as core contributions explaining area-specific differences and reconciling contradictory experimental results. Treated as valuable insights rather than questioned.

Perfect agreement on stimulus-number dependency claims C46-C48. Both accept these as supported findings and testable predictions. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of the paper's contribution to making new experimental predictions.

Perfect agreement on learning trajectory predictions C49, C51-C52. Both accept these as supported by mathematical analysis and consistent with experimental data. Peer reviewers treat this as part of the model's explanatory power without challenge.

Agreement on context-dependent task claims C56-C57 (with C58-C59 in both). OpenEval finds them supported by simulation data and parameter variation. Peer reviewers explicitly accept category and context selectivity profiles as key findings, treating robustness as established.

Agreement on selectivity robustness claims C58-C59. Both accept these as supported by simulation data and consistent with experiments. Peer reviewers group with C56-C57 and treat as extension of core selectivity findings to complex tasks.

Agreement on task-dependent correlation claims C60-C61 (with C73 in peer result). Both accept parameter-dependent correlation behavior. Peer reviewers treat changes with task complexity as part of the explanatory framework for experimental variability.

Disagreement on mechanistic claims C62-C63, C67. OpenEval finds them supported by mathematical analysis. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting 'more intuitive explanations' for context selectivity emergence, calling it 'the most unexpected of the results.'

Disagreement on mechanistic interpretation claims C68-C71. OpenEval finds them supported by mathematical analysis and citations. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the mechanism, questioning dependence on gradient descent versus general loss minimization.

Agreement on task complexity effects claim C73. OpenEval finds it supported by supplementary analysis. Peer reviewers group with C60-C61 and accept as part of the parameter-dependent correlation framework.

Agreement on initial connectivity predictions C74, C76-C78. Both accept these as supported predictions. Peer reviewers acknowledge them as part of new experimental predictions, accepting the mechanistic explanation linking initial conditions to selectivity outcomes.

Agreement on selectivity pattern predictions C79-C81. OpenEval finds them supported by mathematical analysis. Peer reviewers group with C74, C76-C78 and accept as testable predictions without challenge.

Agreement on parameter dependency summary claims C15-C17. OpenEval finds them supported by systematic analysis throughout the paper. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'compelling evidence' that selectivity profiles depend on network details.

Peer reviewers request clarification about context implementation (C53, C55), asking 'how you implemented the context.' This is a request for better explanation rather than a challenge to validity. No corresponding OpenEval result addresses this specific methodological clarification.
